Watching the latest episode of the Cafe Rise made me think couple of stuff:


the license node NFT should come with utility by definition. Once acquired, it is automatically delegated randomly to an active public pool. From a compliance point of view this is ok as the user has to click on “redeem” before receiving any funds and no tax events are created otherwise. Additionally, if the user wants to, the delegation to a pool can be changed to any pool (private or public) as it is now. This would solve the issue of having ~33% of nodes currently inactive.
,


Rob mentioned that there are not enough public pools. While this might be true (they have more data than me) if I scroll through the public pools, I see many pools that are not full. Many spots are still available with good pools sitting at 10/50. My first point would solve this.
,


Maybe we should get rid of the Strength indicator (at least from publicly visible, could still be privately visible to pool operators), might be misleading, let me explain! Some pools have high client success rate, some even 98-99% and still showing only 3 bars in the strength. From a node owner perspective, that is what you want to see (the pool is up and not missing attestations). That “Strength” indicator might mislead a node owner that doesn’t fully know that in that indicator other parameters go into play. Therefore, pools that are at the bottom of the list struggle to get any delegates. My first point would also solve this.
,

Curious to see what others think about this !!

It does come with utility, but the owner needs to use it.  By auto-assigning it, those rewards might be going into a black hole where they should be going to those who at least pay enough attention to take the basic step of delegation.  I don't think this issue lays with anyone who is currently buying Nodes.  It's with those who bought previously and either lost touch or abandoned the project.  I wouldn't want to see rewards siphoned off into accounts that really don't deserve them.  They also may never be claimed.  Better to keep rewards flowing to those who support the project.
,


I'm curious what metrics are being used and what thresholds are being used to make the statement "We don't have enough Public Pools" or even perhaps "We don't have enough Pools, Public and Private."  Those statements confuse me as I don't understand their logical basis.
,

Almost all of my Pools are FULL in terms of delegation, but even so, their capacity to serve files is not even close to being fully utilized.  If there is a concern for being able to handle increased traffic, they should try sending more traffic to those servers that can handle it before concluding that the current network is somehow maxed out and we need more capacity.  Without that benchmark, it seems they really don't know the true capacity of the current network to make such conclusions. ... So, again, how is this being measured to reach the conclusion?


The Strength indicator is not tied to how rewards are distributed.  I agree.  It's very misleading.
,
